deal_summary: A returning customer revised the packaging-line scope and compared suppliers while waiting on funding; the process advanced to contract/invoice work, and the seller later reported receiving payment while EDI signatures were still being sent (evidence 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5).

customer_need.summary: A manager log describes an updated filling/packaging project with a 19-liter option; later offers removed a date coder and compared automatic and semi-automatic packaging (evidence 0, 2).

deal_dynamics.early: The seller sent updated quotes and videos for the returning customer's project (evidence 0, 1).
deal_dynamics.middle: The manager recorded competitor comparison and pending funding; the customer kept refining the equipment and payment format (evidence 2, 3).
deal_dynamics.late: The seller sent contract and invoice documents; on September 7 a seller message said payment was received and documents were sent for EDI signing (evidence 4, 5).

positive_signals: The customer returned to discuss the project, exchanged company details, and continued technical review (evidence 0, 3, 4).
The customer asked a final technical question and responded to the EDI document message (evidence 4, 5).
negative_signals: Funding and competitor comparison delayed a firm decision, according to manager records (evidence 2, 3).
customer_behavior.initiative: The customer considered alternative configurations and supplied legal/company details needed for contract preparation (evidence 2, 3).
customer_behavior.decision_process: The purchase depended on funding, a competitor comparison, and company/legal paperwork; the final EDI signature state is not shown (evidence 2, 3, 4, 5).

strong_actions: The seller changed the proposal as packaging scope changed and sent supporting videos (evidence 1, 2).
The seller prepared contract and invoice documents and routed them through EDI (evidence 4, 5).
weak_actions: The payment/tax format required repeated rework; a manager worklog says a no-VAT offer was available only for cash and the customer wanted bank transfer (evidence 3).
manager_behavior.follow_up_quality: The seller stayed engaged through technical revisions, funding questions, paperwork, and payment tracking (evidence 2, 4, 5).
manager_behavior.next_step_control: The seller said payment was received and sent documents for EDI signature; signature and production start were still unconfirmed in the visible record (evidence 5).

turning_points.description: The customer returned to the project with an expanded packaging option (evidence 0).
The quote changed to remove the date coder and include automatic and semi-automatic packaging options (evidence 2).
The customer supplied company details and the seller sent the contract and invoice package (evidence 3, 4).
The seller reported payment received and sent documents through EDI (evidence 5).

primary_trajectory_explanation.category: funding and configuration changes followed by contract processing
primary_trajectory_explanation.explanation: The trajectory combined changing packaging requirements with delayed funding and supplier comparison. It reached a seller-reported payment and EDI-document stage, but the view does not confirm bank settlement, signatures, production, or delivery (evidence 2, 3, 4, 5).

secondary_factors: A manager log records a mismatch between the customer's preferred bank transfer and a cash-only no-VAT quote option; this remains a worklog claim (evidence 3).
The customer had not settled all technical details when paperwork began (evidence 4).

what_could_be_done: Confirm the final configuration and legal payment basis before preparing contract documents (evidence 2, 3, 4).
Track payment receipt, EDI signature, and production release as separate milestones (evidence 5).
limits: Funding availability and customer payment method were not fully controlled by the seller (evidence 2, 3).
The record ends before EDI completion or delivery is confirmed (evidence 5).

uncertainties: Funding and payment-format details come partly from manager worklogs, not independent customer or bank records (evidence 2, 3).
The September 7 payment message is a seller report; no bank statement or signed EDI document appears in the view (evidence 5).
The exact final equipment package and any production outcome remain uncertain (evidence 2, 4, 5).

evidence.paraphrase: Manager log says a returning customer is updating a project and is considering a 19-liter packaging option.
Seller sends a revised offer adding a compliance-label applicator and a date printer.
Seller sends a revised proposal with the date coder removed and automatic and semi-automatic packaging options added.
Manager worklog says the no-VAT option was limited to cash without documents and the customer preferred a bank transfer; this is a worklog claim.
Seller tells the customer that the contract and invoice package was sent and describes the equipment execution.
Seller message says payment was received and EDI documents were sent for signature; this is not bank evidence.
